Let
\[
v^2=\eta\gamma|A|^2=\eta q\mu D.
\]
Alice and Bob apply the local success filters
\[
F_A=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sqrt s),
\qquad
F_R=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt s\,v,1,0,\ldots,0).
\tag{6}
\]
Each is a finite flag-ancilla dilation. Bob rejects receiver levels \(2,\ldots,N-1\). A known phase correction fixes the Bell-state convention.

For the moment, use an oscillator as a proof device. In the component where all final traveling fields are vacuum, the zero- and one-excitation source operators are exactly
\[
e^{-\mu/2}U_S(\tau)
\left[I|0_R\rangle-v\tau_+^X|1_R\rangle\right].
\]
After (6), the two paths contributing to entanglement leave the source in the same state. Tracing out the source gives a Bell component of weight
\[
\boxed{p_0=e^{-\mu}s\,v^2
=e^{-\mu}s\eta q\mu D}
\tag{7}
\]
and an orthogonal product component of weight \((s/2)p_0\).

The vacuum component is used only in the proof. **The protocol does not condition on observing vacuum in inaccessible fields.**

### Why weak drive does not destroy the fidelity bound

A crude bound by the probability of “any extra photon” loses the transition cancellation and becomes useless as \(\Omega/\gamma\to0\). The exact source correlation retains it.

The source marginal is \(I/2\), which is stationary. Define
\[
C(t)=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[Z\,e^{t\mathcal L}(Z/2)\right].
\]
Its equations are
\[
C''+2\gamma C'+\Omega^2C=0,
\qquad C(0)=1,\quad C'(0)=0.
\]
Since
\[
C'(t)=-\Omega^2\int_0^t e^{-2\gamma(t-u)}C(u)\,du,
\]
we have \(|C'(t)|\le\Omega^2t\). Comparing with the undamped solution gives
\[
\boxed{
|C(t)-\cos\Omega t|
\le\frac{\gamma\Omega^2t^3}{3}.

\tag{8}

\tag{9}
\]
